<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{GenGORZcor1}
 If $\{a(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ satisfies {\rm{\ref{GenGORZThm1assump1}}} with $0\le j\le m$ and {\rm{\ref{GenGORZThm1assump2}}}, then $J^{m,n}_{a}$ is hyperbolic for $n\gg 1$.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- conjecture-1: body_md -->
\label{conj0}
 {\it For $k\ge 2$, $\overline{p}_k(n)$ satisfies \eqref{log-concave} and \eqref{HigherOrderTuranDef} for $n\gg 1$.}
<!-- end conjecture-1 -->
<!-- conjecture-2: body_md -->
\label{conj1}
{\it 	For $k\in \mathbb{N}_{\ge 3}$ and $m\in \mathbb{N}$, the Jensen polynomials $J^{m,n}_{b_k}$ are hyperbolic for $n\!\gg\!1$.}
<!-- end conjecture-2 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{ConjThm1} 
Conjectures \ref{conj0} and \ref{conj1} hold.
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{genthm}
	Let $\{a(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ satisfy {\rm{\ref{GenGORZThm1assump1}}} with $|j|\le \mathcal{C}$, {\rm{\ref{GenGORZThm1assump2}}}, and {\rm{\ref{genthmassump2}}} and assume {\rm{\ref{assump0}}} and {\rm{\ref{assump1}}}. Then we have                                                       
	\begin{align*}
	&I^{[\bm{M}]}_{\bm{\rho},\bm{s}}(a)(n)\sim \frac{D_N}{N!}\mathcal{M}^N(n)\ \ \left(\text{as}\ n\to\infty\right).
	\end{align*}
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{Corgenthm}
	Let $\{a_d(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ be as in \eqref{genexample} and assume {\rm{\ref{assump0}}} and {\rm{\ref{assump1}}}.           
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item \label{Corgenthmeqn1}	For $T\ge 2$, we have, as $n\to \infty$,
		\[
		\mathcal{D}^{[\bm{M}]}_{\bm{\rho},\bm{s}}(a_d)(n)\sim \frac{\left(-\!\lambda^*(1-\lambda^*)\hspace{0.05 cm}A_{\lambda^*}(d)\right)^N\! D_N\hspace{0.05 cm}c^T_1(d)}{2^N N!}\frac{\exp\left(T\sum_{\lambda\in \mathcal{S}}A_{\lambda}(d)n^{\lambda}\right)}{n^{Tc_2(d)+\left(2-\lambda^*\right)N}}.
		\]
		\item \label{Corgenthmeqn2} For $T=1$, we have, as $n\to \infty$,
		\[
		\mathcal{D}^{[\bm{M}]}_{\bm{\rho},\bm{s}}(a_d)(n)\sim \frac{\left(\lambda^*A_{\lambda^*}(d)\right)^N\! D_N\hspace{0.05 cm}c_1(d)}{N! }\frac{\exp\left(\sum_{\lambda\in \mathcal{S}}A_{\lambda}(d)n^{\lambda}\right)}{n^{c_2(d)+\left(1-\lambda^*\right)N}}.
		\]
	\end{enumerate}
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- conjecture-3: body_md -->
{\rm{(\cite[Conjecture 3.11]{LZ})}}\label{LZconj}
{\it  For $k\in \mathbb{N}_{\ge 2}$, $p_k(n)$ and $\overline{p}_k(n)$ satisfy \eqref{Briggsineq} for $n\!\gg\!1$.}
<!-- end conjecture-3 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
\label{Briggsptnoverptnk}
Conjecture \ref{LZconj} is true.
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
\label{newlem1}
 Let $\{a(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ satisfy {\rm{\ref{GenGORZThm1assump1}}} with $|j|\le 2r$, {\rm{\ref{GenGORZThm1assump2}}}, and {\rm{\ref{genthmassump2}}}. Then we have 
	\[
	L_r(a)(n)\sim (2r-1)!!2^{2r-1} {\delta}^{2r}(n)a^2(n)
	\ \ (\text{as}\ \ n\rightarrow\infty).
	\]
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- conjecture-4: body_md -->
\label{Banconj}
{\it We have},\footnote{The factor $n^{-\frac{3r}{2}}$ was missing in \cite{Ban}.} {\it as} $n\to \infty$,
\[
L_r(p)(n)\sim \frac{(2r-1)!!\pi^r }{2^{\frac r2+5} 3^{\frac r2+1}}\frac{e^{2\pi\sqrt{\frac{2}3 n}}}{n^{\frac{3r}{2}+2}}.
\]
<!-- end conjecture-4 -->
<!-- conjecture-5: body_md -->
\label{Mconj1}
{\it We have, as} $n\to \infty$,
\[
L_r\left(p_{24}\right)(n)\sim (2r-1)!!2^{r-2}\pi^r\frac{e^{8\pi\sqrt n}}{n^{\frac{3r+27}2}}.
\]
<!-- end conjecture-5 -->
<!-- theorem-6: body_md -->
\label{ex1}
Conjecture \ref{Banconj} and Conjecture \ref{Mconj1} are true.
<!-- end theorem-6 -->
<!-- conjecture-6: body_md -->
\label{brokenLagconj1}
{\it For $k\in\{1,2\}$ and $1\le r\le 14$, $\{b_k(n)\}_{n\ge N_{b_k}(r)}$ satisfies}\footnote{The values of $N_{b_k}(r)$  for $k\in\{1,2\}$, $1\le r\le 14$ were stated in \cite[Conjecture 6.2]{Yang1}.} \eqref{Lagineq}.
<!-- end conjecture-6 -->
<!-- theorem-7: body_md -->
\label{brokenLagthm1}
 For $k,r\in \mathbb{N}$, we have, as $n\to \infty$, 
	\[
	L_r(b_k)(n)\sim  
	\frac{(2r-1)!!\pi^r (5k+2)^{\frac{r+3}{2}} }{2^{\frac{r+13}{2}} 3^{\frac{r+3}{2}} (2k+1)^{\frac{r+3}{2}} }\frac{e^{2\pi\sqrt{\frac{2(5k+2)}{3(2k+1)}n}}}{n^{\frac{3r+5}{2}}}.
	\]
<!-- end theorem-7 -->
<!-- theorem-8: body_md -->
\label{newsec4lem1}	
	Let $\{a(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ satisfy {\rm{\ref{GenGORZThm1assump1}}} with $|j|\le h r$, {\rm{\ref{GenGORZThm1assump2}}}, and {\rm{\ref{genthmassump2}}}. For $r,h\in \mathbb{N}$, 
	\[
	\Delta^{[r]}_h(a)(n)\sim h^rA^r(n) a(n)\ \ \text{ as}\ \ n\rightarrow\infty.
	\]
<!-- end theorem-8 -->
<!-- theorem-9: body_md -->
\label{mshiftthm}
As $n\to \infty$, we have 
	\[
	\Delta^{[r]}_{h}\left(\textup{pp}\right)(n)\sim C_1\left(\frac{2h A}{3}\right)^r\frac{ e^{A n^{\frac 23}} }{n^{\frac r3+\frac{25}{36}}},
	\]
with $C_1:=\frac{\zeta(3)^{\frac{7}{36}}e^{\zeta'(-1)}}{2^{\frac{11}{36}}\sqrt{3\pi}}$, $A:=\frac{3\zeta(3)^{\frac 13}}{2^{\frac 23}}$, where $\zeta$ is the Riemann zeta function.
<!-- end theorem-9 -->
<!-- conjecture-7: body_md -->
\label{Yangconj}
{\it For $1\le r\le 5$, $\{\Delta^{[r]}(p)(n)\}_{n\ge T_p(r)}$ and $\{\Delta^{[r]}(\overline{p})(n)\}_{n\ge T_{\overline{p}}(r)}$ satisfy}\footnote{The values of $T_p(r)$ and  $T_{\overline{p}}(r)$ were given in \cite[Table 5]{Yang}.} \eqref{HigherOrderTuranDef}.
<!-- end conjecture-7 -->
<!-- theorem-10: body_md -->
\label{Jensencor1}
	Let $r\in \mathbb{N}$. Then $\Delta^{[r]}(p)(n)$ and $\Delta^{[r]}(\overline{p})(n)$ satisfy \eqref{HigherOrderTuranDef} for $n\!\gg\!1$.
<!-- end theorem-10 -->
<!-- conjecture-8: body_md -->
\label{Yangconj1}
{\it For $1\le m\le 11$ and $1\le r\le 5$, $\{\Delta^{[r]}(p)(n)\}_{n\ge L_p(r,m)}$ and}\ \ $\{\Delta^{[r]}(\overline{p})(n)\}_{n\ge L_{\overline{p}}(r,m)}$ {\it satisfy}\footnote{The values for $(L_{p}(r,m))_{\substack{1\le m\le 11\\1\le r\le 5}}$ and $(L_{\overline{p}}(r,m))_{\substack{1\le m\le 11\\1\le r\le 5}}$ were stated in \cite[Table 1 and 2]{Yang}.} \eqref{Lagineq}.
<!-- end conjecture-8 -->
<!-- theorem-11: body_md -->
\label{Lagthm1}
	For $m, r\in \mathbb{N}$, we have, as $n\to \infty$,
	\begin{align*}
	L_m\left(\Delta^{[r]}(p)\right)(n)&\sim                                                                                                        
	\frac{(2m-1)!!\pi^{2r+m}}{2^{r+\frac m2+5}3^{r+\frac m2+1} }\frac{e^{2\pi\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}n}}}{n^{r+\frac{3m}{2}+2}},\\
	L_m\left(\Delta^{[r]}(\overline{p})\right)(n)&\sim                                                                                       
	\frac{(2m-1)!!\pi^{2r+m}}{2^{2r+m+7} }\frac{e^{2\pi\sqrt{n}}}{n^{r+\frac{3m}{2}+2}}.
	\end{align*}
<!-- end theorem-11 -->
<!-- theorem-12: body_md -->
\label{InflogconcaveThm}
 Let $\{a(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ satisfy {\rm{\ref{GenGORZThm1assump1}}} with $|j|\le 2$, {\rm{\ref{GenGORZThm1assump2}}}, {\rm{\ref{genthmassump2}}}, and $\{{\delta}(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ satisfy {\rm{\ref{InflogconcaveThmassump1}}} with $j=\pm 1$, {\rm{\ref{InflogconcaveThmassump2}}}, and {\rm{\ref{InflogconcaveThmassump3}}}. We have, as $n\to \infty$, 
	\[
	\mathcal{L}^{[r]}(a)(n) \sim 2^{2^{r+1}-r-2}{\delta}(n)^{2^{r+1}-2} a^{2^r}\!(n).
	\]
<!-- end theorem-12 -->
<!-- conjecture-9: body_md -->
\label{Banconj1}
{\it We have, as} $n\to \infty$, 
\[
\mathcal{L}^{[r]}(p)(n)\sim \frac{ \pi^{2^r-1}}{2^{5\cdot 2^{r-1}+r-\frac 12} 3^{2^r-\frac 12}}\frac{ e^{2^r\pi\sqrt{\frac{2}3 n}}}{n^{2^r+3\cdot 2^{r-1}-\frac 32}}. 
\]
<!-- end conjecture-9 -->
<!-- theorem-13: body_md -->
\label{inflogthm1} 
Conjecture \ref{Banconj1} is true.
<!-- end theorem-13 -->
<!-- theorem-14: body_md -->
\label{detthm}
	Let $\{a(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ satisfy {\rm{\ref{GenGORZThm1assump1}}} with $|j|\le r-1$ $(r\in \mathbb{N}_{\ge 2})$ and {\rm{\ref{GenGORZThm1assump2}}}. 
	Then we have                      
	\[
	\operatorname{T}^{[r]}_a(n)\sim \frac{(r-1)!^r2^{\frac{r(r-1)}{2}}}{\prod_{j=2}^{r-1}j^{j}}{\delta}^{r(r-1)}(n)a^{r}(n)\ \ (\text{as}\ n\to \infty). 
	\]
<!-- end theorem-14 -->
<!-- conjecture-10: body_md -->
\label{Detconj1}
{\it 	For $k\in \mathbb{N}_{\ge 2}$, we have $\operatorname{T}^{[r]}_p(n)>0$ for $n\!\gg\!1$}.
<!-- end conjecture-10 -->
<!-- theorem-15: body_md -->
\label{detpn}
	As $n\to \infty$, we have 
	\[
	\operatorname{T}^{[r]}_{p}(n)\sim                                                                                                                 
	\frac{(r-1)!^r\pi^{\frac{r(r-1)}{2}}}{2^{\frac{3r^2+5r}{4}}3^{\frac{r(r+1)}{4}}\prod_{j=2}^{r-1}j^{j}}\frac{e^{\pi r\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}n}}}{n^{\frac{3r^2+r}{4}}}.
	\]
<!-- end theorem-15 -->
<!-- theorem-16: body_md -->
\label{detopn}
	As $n\to \infty$, we have 
	\[
	\operatorname{T}^{[r]}_{\overline{p}}(n)\sim                                                         
	\frac{(r-1)!^r\pi^{\frac{r(r-1)}{2}}}{2^{r^2+2r}\prod_{j=2}^{r-1}j^{j}}\frac{e^{\pi r\sqrt{n}}}{n^{\frac{3r^2+r}{4}}}.
	\]
<!-- end theorem-16 -->
<!-- conjecture-11: body_md -->
\cite[Conjecture 6.3]{Yang1}\label{Detconj3}
{\it For $k\!\in\!\{1,2\}$ and $1\!\le\!r\!\le\!14$, $\operatorname{T}^{[r]}_{b_k}(n)>0$ for}\hspace{0.05 cm}\footnote{The values of $(N_{b_k}(r))_{\substack{1\le k\le 2\\1\le r\le 14}}$ were given in \cite[Conjecture 6.3]{Yang1}.} $n\ge N_{b_k}(r)$.
<!-- end conjecture-11 -->
<!-- conjecture-12: body_md -->
\cite[Conjecture 5.1 (2)]{Yang}\label{Detconj4}
{\it For $1\le r\le 11$ and $1\le k\le 5$, $\operatorname{T}^{[r]}_{\Delta^{[k]}(p)}(n), \operatorname{T}^{[r]}_{\Delta^{[k]}(\overline{p})}(n)>0$ for}\footnote{The values of $(D_p(k,r))_{\substack{1\le r\le 11\\1\le k\le 5}}$ and $(D_{\overline{p}}(k,r))_{\substack{1\le r\le 11\\1\le k\le 5}}$ were given in \cite[Table 3 and Table 4]{Yang}.} {\it $n\ge D_p(k,r)$ and $n\ge D_{\overline{p}}(k,r)$, respectively, except if both $k\ge 3$ and $r$ are odd}.
<!-- end conjecture-12 -->
<!-- theorem-17: body_md -->
\label{detbpn}
As $n\to \infty$, we have 
\begin{align*}
\operatorname{T}^{[r]}_{b_k}(n)&\sim \frac{(r-1)!^r\pi^{\frac{r(r-1)}{2}} (5k+2)^{\frac{r^2}{4}+\frac r2}}{2^{\frac{3r^2}{4}+2r}3^{\frac{r^2}{4}+\frac r2}(2k+1)^{\frac{r^2}{4}+\frac r2}\prod_{j=2}^{r-1}j^{j}}
\frac{e^{\pi r\sqrt{\frac{2(5k+2)}{3(2k+1)}n}}}{n^{\frac{3r^2}{4}+\frac r2}},\\
\operatorname{T}^{[r]}_{\Delta^{[k]}(p)}(n)&\sim \frac{(r-1)!^r\pi^{\frac{r(r-1)}{2}+kr}}{2^{\frac{3r^2+\left(2k+5\right)r}{4}}3^{\frac{r^2+(2k+1)r}{4}}\prod_{j=2}^{r-1}j^{j}}                                                                                                                   
\frac{e^{\pi r\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}n}}}{n^{\frac{3r^2+(2k+1)r}{4}}},\\
\operatorname{T}^{[r]}_{\Delta^{[k]}(\overline{p})}(n)&\sim \frac{(r-1)!^r\pi^{\frac{r(r-1)}{2}+kr}}{2^{r^2+(k+2)r}\prod_{j=2}^{r-1}j^{j}} \frac{e^{\pi r\sqrt{n}}}{n^{\frac{3r^2+(2k+1)r}{4}}}.
\end{align*}
<!-- end theorem-17 -->
<!-- theorem-18: body_md -->
\label{itlagthm1}
 Let $\{a(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ satisfy {\rm{\ref{GenGORZThm1assump1}}} with $|j|\le 2r$, {\rm{\ref{GenGORZThm1assump2}}}, {\rm{\ref{genthmassump2}}} and $\{{\delta}(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ satisfy {\rm{\ref{InflogconcaveThmassump1}}} with $j=\pm 1$, {\rm{\ref{InflogconcaveThmassump2}}}, and {\rm{\ref{InflogconcaveThmassump3}}}. Then, for $k\in \mathbb{N}_0$ and $r\in \mathbb{N}$, we have, as $n\to \infty$,                                             
	\[
	L^{[k]}_1\left(L_r(a)\right)(n)\sim (2r-1)!!^{2^k}2^{ 2^{k+1}\left(r+1\right)-k-3}{\delta}(n)^{2^{k+1}\left(r+1\right)-2} a^{2^{k+1}}(n).                                                                                                   
	\]
<!-- end theorem-18 -->
<!-- conjecture-13: body_md -->
\label{DTWConj}
{\it Let $a(n)\in \{p(n),\overline{p}(n),\textup{spt}(n)\}$. For $n\!\gg\!1$ and $k,r\in\mathbb{N}$, $	L^{[k]}_1\left(L_r(a)\right)(n)>0$.}
<!-- end conjecture-13 -->
<!-- theorem-19: body_md -->
\label{itlagthm3}
	As $n\to \infty$, we have
	\begin{align*}
	L^{[k]}_1\left(L_r(p)\right)(n)&\sim \frac{(2r-1)!!^{2^k}\pi^{2^k(r+1)-1}}{2^{2^{k-1}\left(r+9\right)+k+\frac 12}3^{2^{k-1}\left(r+3\right)-\frac 12}}\frac{e^{2^{k+1}\pi\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}n}}}{n^{2^{k-1}\left(3r+7\right)-\frac 32}},\\                                                                                                                                                                                                         
	L^{[k]}_1\left(L_r(\overline{p})\right)(n)&\sim \frac{(2r-1)!!^{2^k}\pi^{2^k(r+1)-1}}{2^{2^k\left(r+7\right)+k}}\frac{e^{2^{k+1}\pi\sqrt{n}}}{n^{2^{k-1}\left(3r+7\right)-\frac 32}},\\                                                                                                                                              
	L^{[k]}_1\left(L_r(\textup{spt})\right)(n)&\sim \frac{(2r-1)!!^{2^k}\pi^{2^k(r-1)-1}}{2^{2^{k-1}\left(r+7\right)+k+\frac 12}3^{2^{k-1}\left(r+1\right)-\frac 12}}\frac{e^{2^{k+1}\pi\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}n}}}{n^{2^{k-1}\left(3r+5\right)-\frac 32}}.                                                                                                                                                                                                      
	\end{align*}	
 In particular, Conjecture \ref{DTWConj} is true.
<!-- end theorem-19 -->
<!-- conjecture-14: body_md -->
\label{brokenlogdiffconj}
{\it For $k, r\!\in\!\mathbb{N}$, there exists $N_k(r)\in\mathbb{N}$ such that                                                                           
	$
	(-1)^{r+1}\Delta^{[r]}(\log(b_k))(n)>0$ for $n\ge N_k(r)$.}
<!-- end conjecture-14 -->
<!-- theorem-20: body_md -->
\label{logdiffconj1}
	Let $r,k\in \mathbb{N}$. Then we have, as $n\to \infty$, 
	\[
	(-1)^{r+1}\Delta^{[r]}\left(\log(b_k)\right)(n)\sim                                                                       
	\frac{\pi(2r-3)!!\sqrt{5k+2}}{2^{r-\frac 12} \sqrt{3\left(2k+1\right)}}n^{\frac 12-r}.
	\]
<!-- end theorem-20 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{sec0prop1}                            
	Let $B(q)=\sum_{n\ge 0}b(n)q^n$ have radius of convergence at least one with $\{b(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ non-negative and weakly increasing. Assume $\lambda,\beta,\gamma\in \mathbb{R}$ with $\gamma>0$ exists with
	\begin{equation}\label{sec0prop1eqn1}
	B\left(e^{-t}\right)\sim \lambda t^{\beta}e^{\frac \gamma t}\ \text{ as}\ t\to 0^{+},\quad B\left(e^{-z}\right)\ll |z|^\beta e^{\frac{\gamma}{|z|}}\ \ \text{ as}\ \ z\to 0,
	\end{equation}
	with the later condition holding in each region $R_{\Delta}$ for $\Delta\ge 0$. Then we have
	\[
	b(n)\sim \frac{\lambda \gamma^{\frac \beta2+\frac 14}}{2\sqrt{\pi}n^{\frac \beta2+\frac 34}}e^{2\sqrt{\gamma n}}\ \text{ as}\ n\to \infty.
	\]
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{elem}
Let $\{a(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ satisfy $a(0)=1$ and set $A(q):=\sum_{n\ge 0}a(n)q^n$. If $(1-q)A(q)$ has non-negative Fourier coefficients, then $\{a(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ is weakly increasing.
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{sec0lem1}                                              
	Let $q=e^{-z}$ and $\Delta\ge 0$. Then, as $z\to 0$ in $R_{\Delta}$, we have
	\[
	(q;q)_{\infty}\sim \sqrt{\frac{2\pi}{z}}e^{-\frac{\pi^2}{6z}}.
	\]
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- theorem-21: body_md -->
\cite[Theorem 3]{GORZ}\label{GORZThm1}
	Let $\{a(n)\}_{n\ge 0}, \{A(n)\}_{n\ge 0}, \{{\delta}(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ be sequences of positive numbers with $\lim_{n\to \infty}{\delta}(n)=0$. Assume that for some $m\in \mathbb{N}$ and all $0\le j\le m$, we have
	\begin{equation*}                     
	\log\left(\frac{a(n+j)}{a(n)}\right)=A(n)j-{\delta}^2(n)j^2+\sum_{k=3}^{m}A_k(n)j^k+o\left({\delta}^{m}(n)\right)\ \ \text{ as}\ \ n\to \infty,
	\end{equation*}
 and $A_k(n)=o({\delta}^k(n))$ as $n\to \infty$. Then we have, locally uniformly in $x$,
	\[
	\lim_{n\to \infty}\frac{J^{m,n}_{a}\left(\frac{{\delta}(n)x-1}{e^{A(n)}}\right)}{a(n){\delta}^{m}(n)}=H_m\left(\frac x2\right).
	\]
<!-- end theorem-21 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
\cite[Corollary 4]{GORZ}\label{GORZcor1}
	The Jensen polynomials $J^{m,n}_{a}$ for a sequence $\{a(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ satisfying the conditions of \Cref{GORZThm1} are hyperbolic for $n\!\gg\!1$.
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{useful}
For $n,t\in\mathbb{N}$, we have         
\begin{equation*}               
\sum_{k=0}^{n}(-1)^k\left(\begin{smallmatrix}n\\\\k\end{smallmatrix}\right)k^t=\begin{cases}
0&\ \text{if}\ \ t<n,\\
(-1)^n n!&\ \text{if}\ \ t=n.
\end{cases}
\end{equation*}
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- theorem-22: body_md -->
\label{GenGORZThm1}
	Let $\{a(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ satisfy {\rm{\ref{GenGORZThm1assump1}}} with $0\le j\le m$ and {\rm{\ref{GenGORZThm1assump2}}}. Then, locally uniformly in $x$, we have
\[
\lim_{n\to \infty}\frac{J^{m,n}_{a}\left(\frac{{\delta}(n)x-1}{e^{A(n)}}\right)}{a(n){\delta}^{m}(n)}=H_m\left(\frac x2\right).
\]
<!-- end theorem-22 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
Using \eqref{Jensendef} and \ref{GenGORZThm1assump1} with $0\le j\le m$, we have  
	\begin{align}\label{Jenseneqn1} 
	&\frac{J^{m,n}_{a}\left(\frac{{\delta}(n)x-1}{e^{A(n)}}\right)}{a(n){\delta}^{m}(n)}
	=\frac{1+o\left(1\right)}{{\delta}^{m}(n)}\left(\sum_{j=0}^{m}\left(\begin{smallmatrix}m\\\\j\end{smallmatrix}\right)\left({\delta}(n)x-1\right)^j+\sum_{j=0}^{m}\left(\begin{smallmatrix}m\\\\j\end{smallmatrix}\right)\sum_{r=1}^{\left\lfloor\frac m2\right\rfloor}\frac{(-1)^r{\delta}^{2r}(n)j^{2r}}{r!}\left({\delta}(n)x-1\right)^j\right.\nonumber\\[-1em]
	&\hspace{7.5 cm}\left.+\sum_{j=0}^{m}\left(\begin{smallmatrix}m\\\\j\end{smallmatrix}\right)\!\!\!\!\!\!\sum_{r\ge \left\lfloor\frac m2\right\rfloor+1}\!\!\!\!\!\frac{(-1)^r{\delta}^{2r}(n)j^{2r}}{r!}\left({\delta}(n)x-1\right)^j\right)\nonumber\\
	&=\left(1+o\left(1\right)\right)\left(x^{m}+\sum_{r=1}^{\left\lfloor\frac m2\right\rfloor}\frac{(-1)^r{\delta}^{2r-m}(n)}{r!}\sum_{j=0}^{m}\left(\begin{smallmatrix}m\\\\j\end{smallmatrix}\right)j^{2r}\left({\delta}(n)x-1\right)^j\right.\nonumber\\[-1.2em]
	&\hspace{5 cm}\left.+{\delta}^{-m}(n)\sum_{j=0}^{m}\left(\begin{smallmatrix}m\\\\j\end{smallmatrix}\right)\!\!\!\!\!\!\sum_{r\ge \left\lfloor\frac m2\right\rfloor+1}\!\!\!\!\!\frac{(-1)^r{\delta}^{2r}(n)j^{2r}}{r!}\left({\delta}(n)x-1\right)^j\right).            
	\end{align}
	
	
	Next, we expand
	\begin{align}\label{Jenseneqn2}
	&x^m+\sum_{r=1}^{\left\lfloor\frac m2\right\rfloor}\frac{(-1)^r{\delta}^{2r-m}(n)}{r!}\sum_{j=0}^{m}\left(\begin{smallmatrix}m\\\\j\end{smallmatrix}\right)j^{2r}\left({\delta}(n)x-1\right)^j\nonumber\\
	&\hspace{1 cm}=x^m+\sum_{r=1}^{\left\lfloor\frac m2\right\rfloor}\frac{(-1)^r}{r!}\sum_{\ell=0}^{m-2r}(-1)^{\ell}{\delta}(n)^{2r-m+\ell}x^{\ell}\sum_{j=\ell}^{m}(-1)^j\left(\begin{smallmatrix}m\\\\j\end{smallmatrix}\right)\left(\begin{smallmatrix}j\\\\\ell\end{smallmatrix}\right)j^{2r}\nonumber\\
	&\hspace{2 cm}+\sum_{r=1}^{\left\lfloor\frac m2\right\rfloor}\frac{(-1)^r}{r!}\sum_{\ell=m-2r+1}^{m}(-1)^{\ell}{\delta}(n)^{2r-m+\ell}x^{\ell}\sum_{j=\ell}^{m}(-1)^j\left(\begin{smallmatrix}m\\\\j\end{smallmatrix}\right)\left(\begin{smallmatrix}j\\\\\ell\end{smallmatrix}\right)j^{2r}.
	\end{align}
Using \eqref{Hermitedef} and \Cref{useful}, the first two terms combine as 
\begin{align*}
x^m+\sum_{r=1}^{\left\lfloor\frac m2\right\rfloor}\frac{(-1)^r}{r!}\sum_{\ell=0}^{m-2r}\left(\begin{smallmatrix}m\\\\\ell\end{smallmatrix}\right){\delta}(n)^{2r-m+\ell}x^{\ell}\sum_{k=0}^{2r}\left(\begin{smallmatrix}2r\\\\k\end{smallmatrix}\right)\ell^{2r-k}\sum_{j=0}^{m-\ell}(-1)^{j}\left(\begin{smallmatrix}m-\ell\\\\j\end{smallmatrix}\right)j^k=H_m\left(\frac x2\right).
\end{align*}
Plugging this into \eqref{Jenseneqn2} and then into \eqref{Jenseneqn1}, we have 
	\begin{align}\label{Jenseneqn5}
	&\frac{J^{m,n}_{a}\left(\frac{{\delta}(n)x-1}{e^{A(n)}}\right)}{a(n){\delta}^{m}(n)}
	=\left(1+o\left(1\right)\right)\left(H_m\left(\frac x2\right)+S^{[1]}_m(n,x)+S^{[2]}_m(n,x)\right),
	\end{align}
	where 
	\begin{align*}                   
	S^{[1]}_m(n,x)&:=\sum_{r=1}^{\left\lfloor\frac m2\right\rfloor}\frac{(-1)^r}{r!}\sum_{\ell=m-2r+1}^{m}(-1)^{\ell}{\delta}(n)^{2r-m+\ell}x^{\ell}\sum_{j=\ell}^{m}(-1)^j\left(\begin{smallmatrix}m\\\\j\end{smallmatrix}\right)\left(\begin{smallmatrix}j\\\\\ell\end{smallmatrix}\right)j^{2r},\nonumber\\                   
	S^{[2]}_m(n,x)&:={\delta}^{-m}(n)\sum_{j=0}^{m}\left(\begin{smallmatrix}m\\\\j\end{smallmatrix}\right)\sum_{r\ge \left\lfloor\frac m2\right\rfloor+1}\frac{\left(-1\right)^r}{r!}{\delta}^{2r}(n)j^{2r}\left({\delta}(n)x-1\right)^j.                     
	                                                                                                                                  
	\end{align*}
Using \ref{GenGORZThm1assump2}, we then bound 	                                  
	\begin{align}\label{Jenseneqn9}
	\left|S^{[1]}_m(n,x)\right|&\le 
	{\delta}(n)\!\sum_{r=1}^{\left\lfloor\frac m2\right\rfloor}\!\frac{m^{2r}}{r!}\!\sum_{\ell=m-2r+1}^{m}\!\left(\begin{smallmatrix}m\\\\\ell\end{smallmatrix}\right)\!|x|^{\ell}\sum_{j=\ell}^{m}\!\left(\begin{smallmatrix}m-\ell\\\\j-\ell\end{smallmatrix}\right)
	=2^m{\delta}(n)\sum_{r=1}^{\left\lfloor\frac m2\right\rfloor}\!\frac{m^{2r}}{r!}\!\sum_{\ell=m-2r+1}^{m}\!\left(\begin{smallmatrix}m\\\\\ell\end{smallmatrix}\right)\left(\frac{|x|}{2}\right)^{\ell}\nonumber\\
	&
	\le 2^m\left(e^{m^2}-1\right)\left(\left(1+\frac{|x|}{2}\right)^m-1\right){\delta}(n)=O_m\left({\delta}(n)\right),
	\end{align}
assuming that $x$ lies in a compact set. Next, using \ref{GenGORZThm1assump2}, we similarly obtain 
	\begin{align*}                    
\left|S^{[2]}_m(n,x)\right|=O_m\left({\delta}(n)\right). 
\end{align*}
Plugging this and \eqref{Jenseneqn9} into \eqref{Jenseneqn5}, and letting $n\to \infty$, we obtain the theorem.\qedhere
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
It is not hard to see that if a sequence of real polynomials $P^{[d]}_n(x)$ of degree $d$ converges locally uniformly to a real polynomial $P_d(x)$ of degree $d$ with only real simple zeros, then $P^{[d]}_{n}$ has only real simple zeros for $n\!\gg\!1$. Applying this to \Cref{GenGORZThm1} and using the fact that $H_m(x)$ has simple real zeros (see \cite[§18.16(v)]{DLMF}), we obtain the claim.\qedhere
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{Nlem1}
 Let $\{a(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ satisfy {\rm{\ref{Nlem1assump2}}}.                                                                                                                
Then, for all $j\in \mathbb{N}_0$, $L_j=1$.
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
Using \ref{Nlem1assump2} and $a(n)>0$ for $n\in \mathbb{N}$,
                                 
$\{\frac{a(n+j)}{a(n)}\}_{n\ge 0}$ is positive and weakly decreasing. Thus 
$L_j\ge 0$. By \ref{Nlem1assump3}, $L_j$ is independent of $j$. Computing $L_0=1$ gives the claim.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
\label{Nlem2}
If $\{a(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ satisfies {\rm{\ref{Nlem1assump2}}}\textendash{\rm{\ref{Nlem2assump1}}}, then it satisfies {\rm{\ref{GenGORZThm1assump1}}} with $0\le j\le m$ and {\rm{\ref{GenGORZThm1assump2}}}.
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
By \Cref{Nlem1} and \ref{Nlem2assump1}, $\lim_{n\to \infty}\psi_n(j)=0$ for all $j\in \mathbb{N}_0$. By \ref{Nlem2assump1}, $\lim_{n\to \infty}c_1(n)=\lim_{n\to \infty}c_2(n)=0$.  Using this and \ref{Nlem2assump1}, $\{a(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ satisfies \ref{GenGORZThm1assump1} with $0\le j\le m$, 
$A(n):=c_1(n)$, and ${\delta}(n):=\sqrt{\frac 12(c^2_1(n)-c_2(n))}$ and by \ref{Nlem2assump1}, $\{{\delta}(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ satisfies \ref{GenGORZThm1assump2}.\qedhere
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- theorem-23: body_md -->
\label{HypEquivthm}
Let $\{a(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ satisfy {\rm{\ref{Nlem1assump3}}} and  {\rm{\ref{Nlem2assump1}}} and assume that,                                            
 for $n\gg1$,
$J^{2,n}_a(x)$ is hyperbolic. Then $J^{m,n}_a(x)$ is hyperbolic for $m\in \mathbb{N}_{\ge 2}$ and $n\!\gg\!1$.
<!-- end theorem-23 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
\label{Fact1}
	If $f(n)\sim g(n)$ as $n\to \infty$, then, for $\alpha_1\le j\le \alpha_2$                                
	 with $j$ fixed, 
	\[
	\log\left(\frac{f(n+j)}{f(n)}\right)=\log\left(\frac{g(n+j)}{g(n)}\right)+o(1)\ \ \text{as}\ \ n\to\infty.
	\]
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- lemma-7: body_md -->
\label{fact2}
Let $\{a_d(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ be as in \eqref{genexample}. 
\begin{enumerate}
	\item \label{fact2part1} The sequence $\{a_d(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ satisfies {\rm{\ref{GenGORZThm1assump1}}} for all $\alpha_1\le j\le \alpha_2$, {\rm{\ref{GenGORZThm1assump2}}}, and {\rm{\ref{genthmassump2}}}.
	\item \label{fact2part2} The sequence $\{{\delta}(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ satisfies {\rm{\ref{InflogconcaveThmassump1}}} for all $\alpha_1\le j\le \alpha_2$, {\rm{\ref{InflogconcaveThmassump2}}}, and {\rm{\ref{InflogconcaveThmassump3}}}. 
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-7 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
From \eqref{genexample} and \Cref{Fact1}, we have,
\begin{align}\label{neweqn9}
\log\left(\frac{a_d(n+j)}{a_d(n)}\right)
&=A(n)j-{\delta}^2(n)j^2+\sum_{\ell\ge 3}A_{\ell}(n)j^\ell+o(1)\ \ \left(\text{ as}\ n\to \infty\right),
\end{align}
                                            
where 
\begin{align*}
A(n)&:=\sum_{\lambda\in \mathcal{S}}\lambda A_{\lambda}(d)n^{\lambda-1}-\frac{c_2(d)}{n},\quad {\delta}(n):=\frac1{\sqrt2n}\sqrt{\sum_{\lambda\in \mathcal{S}}\lambda(1-\lambda) A_{\lambda}(d)n^{\lambda}-c_2(d)},\\
A_{\ell}(n)&:=\sum_{\lambda\in \mathcal{S}}\left(\begin{smallmatrix}\lambda\\\\\ell\end{smallmatrix}\right)A_{\lambda}(d)n^{\lambda-\ell}+\frac{(-1)^\ell c_2(d)}{\ell n^\ell}.
\end{align*}

\noindent \ref{fact2part1} Using \ref{genexampleassump2} and \ref{genexampleassump3}, we have, as $n\to \infty$,  
\begin{equation}\label{obs4}
A(n)\sim \frac{\lambda^*A_{\lambda^*}(d)}{n^{1-\lambda^*}}\to 0.
\end{equation}
                 
   
                                                                                          
    
Thus \ref{genthmassump2} is satisfied. From \ref{genexampleassump3}, we obtain ${\delta}(n)>0$ for $n\!\gg\!1$. Using \ref{genexampleassump3}, we have 
\begin{equation}\label{impfact}
{\delta}(n)\sim \sqrt{\frac{\lambda^*(1-\lambda^*)A_{\lambda^*}(d)}{2}}n^{\frac{\lambda^*}{2}-1}\to 0\ \ \ \ \ \ (\text{as}\ n\to \infty).                                
\end{equation}
 Thus \ref{GenGORZThm1assump2} is satisfied. Next, for  $\alpha_1\le j\le \alpha_2$, we show that
\begin{align}                     
                                                        
                                                                                               
\label{jenseneqn1}
\sum_{\ell\ge 3}A_{\ell}(n)j^\ell&=o\left(1\right).                                            
\end{align}
Using $|(\begin{smallmatrix}\lambda\\\ell\end{smallmatrix})|\le \lambda$ for $\ell\in \mathbb{N}_{\ge 3}$ and \ref{genexampleassump2}\textendash\ref{genexampleassump4}, we estimate, for $\ell\in\mathbb{N}_{\ge 3}$, 
\begin{equation}\label{newlem2eqn3a}
|A_{\ell}(n)| \le \left(\lambda^*\sum_{\lambda\in \mathcal{S}} |A_{\lambda}(d)|+\frac{\left|c_2(d)\right|}{3}\right)n^{\lambda^*-\ell}=:\kappa_d n^{\lambda^*-\ell}.
\end{equation}
 Using \eqref{newlem2eqn3a}, we bound, for $n\!\gg\!1$ (and $n\ge 2K$, where $K:=\max\{|\alpha_1|, |\alpha_2|\}$), 
\begin{align*}
\left|\sum_{\ell\ge 3}A_{\ell}(n)j^\ell\right|&\le \sum_{\ell\ge 3}\left|A_{\ell}(n)\right|K^\ell
\le 2\kappa_{d}K^{3}n^{\lambda^*-3}.
\end{align*}
 Consequently, by \ref{genexampleassump2}, and \ref{genexampleassump3}, we obtain that \eqref{jenseneqn1} holds. Using this and \eqref{neweqn9}, $\{a_d(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ satisfies \ref{GenGORZThm1assump1} with $\alpha_1\le j\le \alpha_2$. This concludes the proof of \ref{fact2part1}. 

\noindent \ref{fact2part2}  By \eqref{impfact} and \Cref{Fact1}, we have                                              
\begin{align}\label{neweqn11}
\log\left(\frac{{\delta}(n+j)}{{\delta}(n)}\right)
&=B(n)j+\beta^2(n)j^2+\sum_{m\ge 3}B_{m}(n)j^m+o(1),
\end{align}
where
\[
B(n):=\left(\frac{\lambda^*}{2}-1\right)\frac 1n,\quad \beta(n):=\sqrt{\frac 12\left(1-\frac{\lambda^*}{2}\right)}\frac 1n,\quad B_m(n)=\left(\frac{\lambda^*}{2}-1\right)\frac{(-1)^{m+1}}{m n^m}.
\]
We have $\lim_{n\to \infty}B(n)=0$ and $\beta(n)=o({\delta}(n))$. Thus \ref{InflogconcaveThmassump2} and \ref{InflogconcaveThmassump3} are satisfied. Note that, for $\alpha_1\le j\le \alpha_2$ and $n\!\gg\!1$,                                                  
\[
\sum_{m\ge 3}B_{m}(n)j^m=o(1).
\] 
Using \eqref{neweqn11}, we see that $\{{\delta}(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ satisfies \ref{InflogconcaveThmassump1} with $\alpha_1\le j\le \alpha_2$.\qedhere
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- lemma-8: body_md -->
\label{sec:Jensenlem1}
	Let $\{a_d(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ be as in \eqref{genexample} and $m\ge 2$. Then $J^{m,n}_{a_d}$ is hyperbolic for $n\gg 1$.
<!-- end lemma-8 -->
<!-- lemma-9: body_md -->
\label{overptnlem1}
	Let $k\ge 2$. We have\footnote{\Cref{overptnlem1} corrects typos from \cite[equation (3.18)]{PZZ}.}
	\[
	\overline{p}_k(n)\sim \frac{\left(k-1\right)^{\frac 14}}{2^{\frac 32}k^{\frac 34} }\frac{e^{\pi\sqrt{\frac{k-1}k n}}}{n^{\frac 34}}\ \ \text{ as}\ \ n\to \infty.
	\]
<!-- end lemma-9 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
We rewrite \eqref{genfunc1} as 
\begin{equation*} 
P_k(q)=\sum_{n\ge 0}\overline{p}_k(n)q^n=\frac{\left(q^2;q^2\right)_{\infty}\left(q^{k};q^{k}\right)^2_{\infty}}{\left(q\right)^2_{\infty}\left(q^{2k};q^{2k}\right)_{\infty}}.
\end{equation*}
By \Cref{sec0lem1}, as $z\to 0$ in $R_{\Delta}$ ($\Delta\ge 0$), 
	\[
	P_k(e^{-z})\sim 
	\frac{e^{\frac{(k-1)\pi^2}{4kz}}}{\sqrt k}.
	\]
	Thus $P_k(q)$ satisfies \eqref{sec0prop1eqn1} with $\lambda=\frac{1}{\sqrt{k}}$, $\beta=0$, and $\gamma=\frac{(k-1)\pi^2}{4k}$. Next, note that $\overline{p}_k(0)=1$. It remains to show that $\{\overline{p}_k(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ is weakly increasing. Using \eqref{genfunc1}, we obtain  
	\begin{align*}
\left(1-q\right)P_k(q)
=\frac{\prod_{1\le j\le k-1}\left(-q^j;q^k\right)_{\infty}}{\left(q^{k+1};q^k\right)_{\infty}\prod_{2\le j\le k-1}\left(q^j;q^k\right)_{\infty}}.
	\end{align*}
Thus $(1-q)P_k(q)$ has non-negative Fourier coefficients and thus, by \Cref{elem}, $\overline{p}_k(n)\ge \overline{p}_k(n-1)$ for $n\in \mathbb{N}$. The claim then follows, using \Cref{sec0prop1}.\qedhere
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- lemma-10: body_md -->
\label{brokenlem1}
	For $k\in \mathbb{N}$, we have 
	\[
	b_k(n)\sim \frac{(5k+2)^{\frac 34}}{2^{\frac{11}4} 3^{\frac 34} (2k+1)^{\frac 34}}\frac{e^{\pi\sqrt{\frac{2(5k+2)}{3(2k+1)}n}}}{n^{\frac 54}}\ \ \text{ as}\ \ n\to \infty.
	\]
<!-- end lemma-10 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
By \Cref{overptnlem1} and \Cref{sec:Jensenlem1}, we conclude the proof of Conjecture \ref{conj0}. By \Cref{brokenlem1} and \Cref{sec:Jensenlem1} of the paper, we obtain Conjecture \ref{conj1}.\qedhere
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
Note that 
 $\mathcal{C}\in \mathbb{N}$. 
For $\ell\in \{1,2\}$, $1\le m\le M_{\ell}$ and $N\in \mathbb{N}$, set 
	\[w_{s_{\ell},m}(n):=-{\delta}^2(n)\sum_{k=1}^{T}s^2_{\ell}(k,m),\quad \phi_N(x):=\sum_{m=1}^{N}\frac{x^m}{m!}.\]
We first assume that $T\ge 2$. Using \eqref{gendefn} and \ref{GenGORZThm1assump1} with $|j|\le \mathcal{C}$, we have, for $\ell\in \{1,2\}$, 
	\begin{align}\label{genthmeqn1}
	\frac{P^{[M_{\ell}]}_{\rho_{\ell},s_{\ell}}(a)(n)}{a^{T}(n)}\!&=\!
\left(1\!+\!o_T\left(1\right)\right)\!\sum_{m=1}^{M_{\ell}}\!\rho_{\ell}(m)e^{A(n)\!\sum_{k=1}^{T}\!s_{\ell}(k,m)}            
                                                                       
\left(\!1\!+\!\phi_{N}\!\left(w_{s_{\ell},m}(n)\right)\!+\!\!\!\!\sum_{t\ge N+1}\!\frac{w^t_{s_{\ell},m}(n)}{t!}\!\right).
	\end{align}
	Bounding $w_{s_{\ell},m}(n)\ll_{C,T} {\delta}^2(n)$,                                                
	we have, for $n\!\gg\!1$,  
	\begin{align*}                   
	\left|\sum_{t\ge N+1}\frac{w^t_{s_{\ell},m}(n)}{t!}\right|
	\le \frac{\left|w^{N+1}_{s_{\ell},m}(n)\right|}{\left(N+1\right)!}\sum_{t\ge 0}\frac{1}{t!}\ll_{\mathcal{C},T,N}{\delta}^{2N+2}(n).	\end{align*}
                                 
Plugging                    
this into \eqref{genthmeqn1}, using \ref{genthmassump2} and \eqref{gendefn}, we have, for $n\!\gg\!1$, 
\begin{align}\label{genthmeqn15}
I^{[\bm{M}]}_{\bm{\rho},\bm{s}}(a)(n)=\left(1\!+\!o_{T}\left(1\right)\right)\Bigl(1+O_{\mathcal{C}, T}\left(A(n)\right)\Bigr)\sum_{\ell=1}^{2}T^{[\ell]}_{\bm{M},N}(n),
\end{align}
where 
	\begin{align*}
	T^{[1]}_{\bm{M},N}(n)&:=\sum_{\ell=1}^2 (-1)^{\ell+1}\sum_{m=1}^{M_{\ell}}\!\rho_{\ell}(m)\phi_N\!\left(-{\delta}^2(n)\!\sum_{k=1}^{T}\!s^2_{\ell}(k,m)\right),\\
	T^{[2]}_{\bm{M},N}(n)&:=\Bigl(1+O_{\mathcal{C},T,N}\left({\delta}^{2N+2}(n)\right)\Bigr)D_0.
	\end{align*}
Using  \ref{assump0}, we have, for $n\!\gg\!1$, 
	\begin{equation}\label{genthmeqn16}
	T^{[2]}_{\bm{M}, N}(n)=0.
	\end{equation}
 Finally, using \eqref{newdef3}, \ref{assump0}, and \ref{assump1}, we have 
	\begin{align*}                    
	T^{[1]}_{\bm{M},N}(n)=\frac{(-1)^ND_N}{N!}{\delta}^{2N}(n).
	\end{align*}
	Plugging this and \eqref{genthmeqn16}                                                     
	into \eqref{genthmeqn15} and using \ref{genthmassump2} we have, for $T\ge 2$, as $n\to \infty$,
	\begin{align*}               
	&I^{[\bm{M}]}_{\bm{\rho},\bm{s}}(a)(n)\sim \frac{(-1)^{N}D_N}{N!}{\delta}^{2N}(n).            
	                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
	\end{align*}	
 This, together with \eqref{newdef2}, concludes the proof of \Cref{genthm} for $T\ge 2$.

Next we let $T=1$. For $\ell\in \{1,2\}$, using \eqref{gendefn}, \ref{GenGORZThm1assump1} with $|j|\le \mathcal{C}$, \ref{GenGORZThm1assump2}, and \ref{genthmassump2}, we have,
\[
\frac{P^{[M_{\ell}]}_{\rho_{\ell},s_{\ell}}(a)(n)}{a(n)}=\left(1\!+\!o_{\mathcal{C}}\left(1\right)\right)\! \sum_{m=1}^{M_{\ell}}\!\rho_{\ell}(m)\!\left(1\!+\!\phi_N\left(A(n)s_{\ell}(1,m)\right)\!+\!O_{\mathcal{C}}\left(A^{2}(n)\right)\right)\ \ \left(\text{as}\ n\to \infty\right).
\]
Thus, using \eqref{gendefn}, \ref{assump0}, and \eqref{newdef3}, we have, as $n\to \infty$,
\[
I^{[\bm{M}]}_{\bm{\rho},\bm{s}}(a)(n)\sim \frac{D_N}{N!}A^N(n).
\]
 Combining this and using \eqref{newdef2}, the claim follows.\qedhere
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
By \Cref{fact2} \ref{fact2part1}, $\{a_d(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ satisfies \ref{GenGORZThm1assump1} with $|j|\le \mathcal{C}$, \ref{GenGORZThm1assump2}, \ref{genthmassump2}. Using \eqref{gendefn1}, \eqref{gendefn}, and \Cref{genthm}, we have
 \begin{equation}\label{nclaim3}
\frac{\mathcal{D}^{[\bm{M}]}_{\bm{\rho},\bm{s}}(a_d)(n)}{a^T_d(n)}\sim \frac{D_N}{N!}\mathcal{M}^N(n). 
 \end{equation}
  

\noindent \ref{Corgenthmeqn1}  By \eqref{nclaim3}, \eqref{newdef2}, and \eqref{impfact}, we have, as $n\to \infty$, 
\[
\frac{\mathcal{D}^{[\bm{M}]}_{\bm{\rho},\bm{s}}(a_d)(n)}{a^T_d(n)}\sim \frac{\left(-\lambda^*(1-\lambda^*)A_{\lambda^*}(d)\right)^N\!D_N }{2^NN!}n^{\left(\lambda^*-2\right)N}.
\]
Using this and \eqref{genexample}, we conclude the proof of \ref{Corgenthmeqn1}. 

\noindent \ref{Corgenthmeqn2} \hspace{-0.05 cm}  The proof is analogous to that of \ref{Corgenthmeqn1}, using \eqref{nclaim3}, \eqref{newdef2}, \eqref{obs4}, and \eqref{genexample}.\qedhere
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- corollary-3: body_md -->
\label{genthmcor1}
Let $\{a_d(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ be as in \eqref{genexample}. Then $a_d(n)$ satisfies \eqref{Briggsineq} for $n\!\gg\!1$.
<!-- end corollary-3 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
To prove \eqref{Briggsineq}, it suffices to show that $\{a_d(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ satisfies \eqref{log-concave} and \eqref{Briggsineq2} for $n\!\gg\!1$. By \Cref{sec:Jensenlem1}, \eqref{log-concave} holds for $\{a_d(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ for $n\!\gg\!1$.  From \ref{Briggsineq3},                    
  we have, using \eqref{newdef3}, $D_2=8$. 
Moreover, by \Cref{fact2} \ref{fact2part1}, $\{a_d(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ satisfies \ref{GenGORZThm1assump1} with $|j|\le 2$, \ref{GenGORZThm1assump2}, and \ref{genthmassump2}. Thus by \Cref{Corgenthm} \ref{Corgenthmeqn1}, we have, as $n\to \infty$, 
	\begin{align*}
	B\left(a_d(n)\right)
	&\sim \left(\lambda^*(1-\lambda^*)A_{\lambda^*}(d)\right)^2c^3_1(d)\frac{\exp\left(3\sum_{\lambda\in \mathcal{S}}A_{\lambda}(d)n^{\lambda}\right)}{n^{3c_2(d)+2\left(2-\lambda^*\right)}}.
	\end{align*}
	This implies that $\{a_d(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ satisfies \eqref{Briggsineq2} for $n\!\gg\!1$ and thus concludes the proof.\qedhere
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
Using the asymptotics of $p_k(n)$ (see \cite[equation (2.1)]{CP}),  \Cref{overptnlem1}, and \Cref{genthmcor1}, we conclude the proof.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
Using \eqref{Lagineq}, we write 
\begin{align*}
&2(-1)^rL_r(a)(n)
=\!\sum_{m=1}^{r+1}\!\left(\begin{smallmatrix}2r\\\\2m-2\end{smallmatrix}\right)\!a(n+2m-2)a(n+2r-2m+2)\nonumber\\[-10 pt]
&\hspace{7 cm}-\sum_{m=1}^{r}\left(\begin{smallmatrix}2r\\\\2m-1\end{smallmatrix}\right)a(n+2m-1)a(n+2r-2m+1).
\end{align*}
 In the notation of \eqref{gendefn1} and \eqref{gendefn}, $T=2$, $M_1=r+1$, $M_2=r$, $\rho_1(m)=(\begin{smallmatrix}2r\\2m-2\end{smallmatrix})$, $\rho_2(m)=(\begin{smallmatrix}2r\\2m-1\end{smallmatrix})$, $s_1(1,m)=2m-2$, $s_1(2,m)=2r-2m+2$, $s_2(1,m)=2m-1$, and $s_2(2,m)=2r-2m+1$. 
Then $\mathcal{C}=2r$. Next, we show that \ref{assump0} and \ref{assump1} are satisfied with $N=r$. We have
\begin{align}\label{obs1}
&              
D_t=\sum_{\ell=0}^{t}\left(\begin{smallmatrix}t\\\\\ell\end{smallmatrix}\right)\sum_{k=0}^{2t-2\ell}\left(\begin{smallmatrix}2t-2\ell\\\\k\end{smallmatrix}\right)(-2r)^k\sum_{m=0}^{2r}(-1)^m\left(\begin{smallmatrix}2r\\\\m\end{smallmatrix}\right)m^{2t-k}.
\end{align}
 By \Cref{useful}, this vanishes for $t<r$. Using \Cref{useful}, \eqref{obs1} equals $2^r(2r)!$ for $t=r$. Thus \ref{assump0} and \ref{assump1} hold with $N=r$ and $D_r=2^r(2r)!$. This concludes the proof.\qedhere
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- corollary-4: body_md -->
\label{newcor1}
Let $\{a_d(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ be as in \eqref{genexample}. We have, as $n\to \infty$, 
\[
L_r(a_d)(n)\sim (2r-1)!!\frac{c_1^2(d)}{2}\left(2\lambda^*(1-\lambda^*)A_{\lambda^*}(d)\right)^r\frac{\exp\left(2\sum_{\lambda\in \mathcal{S}}A_{\lambda}(d)n^{\lambda}\right)}{n^{2c_2(d)+(2-\lambda^*)r}}.                              
\]
<!-- end corollary-4 -->
<!-- corollary-5: body_md -->
\label{ex2}
	With $\alpha>0$ we have, as $n\to \infty$, 
	\[
	L_r(p_{\alpha})(n)\sim \frac{(2r-1)!!\pi^r\alpha^{\frac{\alpha+r+1}{2}} }{ 2^{\frac{3\alpha+r+7}{2}} 3^{\frac{\alpha+r+1}{2}} }\frac{e^{2\pi\sqrt{\frac{2\alpha}3 n}}}{n^{\frac{\alpha+3+3r}{2}}}.
	\]
<!-- end corollary-5 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
From \cite[Corollary 1.2]{IJT}, we have, as $n\to \infty$, 
	\[
	p_\alpha(n)\sim
	\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left(\frac{\alpha}{24}\right)^{\frac{\alpha+1}{4}}\frac{e^{\pi\sqrt{\frac{2\alpha}3 n}}}{n^{\frac{\alpha+3}{4}}}.
	\]
 Applying \Cref{newcor1}, the claim follows.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
Plugging $\alpha=1$ resp. $\alpha=24$ into \Cref{ex2} gives the theorem.\qedhere
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
Plugging \Cref{brokenlem1} into \Cref{newcor1} gives the theorem. \qedhere
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
First, using \eqref{deltadef}, we have, for $r\in \mathbb{N}$,
\begin{align*}
\Delta^{[r]}_h(a)(n)=\sum_{m=1}^{\left\lfloor\frac r2\right\rfloor+1}\left(\begin{smallmatrix}r\\\\2m-2\end{smallmatrix}\right)a\left(n-h(2m-2)\right)-\sum_{m=1}^{\left\lfloor\frac{r+1}{2}\right\rfloor}\left(\begin{smallmatrix}r\\\\2m-1\end{smallmatrix}\right)a\left(n-h(2m-1)\right).
\end{align*}	
 In the notation of \eqref{gendefn} and \eqref{gendefn1}, $T=1$, $M_1=\lfloor\frac{r}{2}\rfloor+1$, $M_2=\lfloor\frac{r+1}{2}\rfloor$, $\rho_1(m)=(\begin{smallmatrix}r\\2m-2\end{smallmatrix})$, $\rho_2(m)=(\begin{smallmatrix}r\\2m-1\end{smallmatrix})$, $s_1(1,m)=-h(2m-2)$, and $s_2(1,m)=-h(2m-1)$. Then, $\mathcal{C}=h r$. Using \Cref{useful} and \eqref{newdef3}, \ref{assump0} and \ref{assump1} hold with $N=r$. Moreover, $D_r=h^rr!$. 
  Using this, \Cref{genthm} with $T=1$ and $N=r$, and \eqref{newdef2}, we conclude the proof.\qedhere
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- corollary-6: body_md -->
\label{newsec4lem3}
 Let $\{a_d(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ be as in \eqref{genexample}. We have, 
	\[
	\Delta^{[r]}_h(a_d)(n)\sim c_1(d)\left(h \lambda^*  A_{\lambda^*}(d)\right)^r \frac{\exp\left(\sum_{\lambda\in \mathcal{S}}  A_{\lambda}(d)n^{\lambda}\right) }{n^{c_2(d)+\left(1-\lambda^*\right)r}}\ \ \text{ as}\ \ n\to \infty.
	\]
<!-- end corollary-6 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
By Wright \cite{Wright}, we have 
\begin{equation*}                   
\textup{pp}(n)\sim C_1\frac{e^{A n^{\frac 23}}}{n^{\frac{25}{36}}}\ \ \text{as}\ \ n\to \infty,
\end{equation*}
where $C_1$ and $A$ are as in \Cref{mshiftthm}. Applying \Cref{newsec4lem3}, the claim follows.\qedhere
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- corollary-7: body_md -->
\label{shiftediffthm}
	We have, as $n\to \infty$, 
\begin{align*}
	\Delta^{[r]}_{h}(p)(n)&\sim
\frac{\pi^r h^r}{2^{\frac r2+2}3^{\frac{r+1}2}}\frac{ e^{\pi\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}n}}}{n^{\frac r2+1}},\qquad 
\Delta^{[r]}_{h}(\overline{p})(n)\sim \frac{\pi^rh^r}{2^{r+3}} \frac{e^{\pi\sqrt{n}}}{n^{\frac r2+1}}.
\end{align*}
<!-- end corollary-7 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
Using \eqref{deltadef}, \Cref{shiftediffthm}, and \Cref{sec:Jensenlem1}, we conclude the proof.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
Using \Cref{newcor1} and \Cref{shiftediffthm}, we conclude the proof.
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
Using \eqref{logdef} and \eqref{Lagineq}, we have  
	\begin{equation}\label{Inflogconcaveeqn1}
	\frac{\mathcal{L}^{[1]}(a)(n+1)}{a^2(n+1)}
	=\frac{L_1(a)(n)}{a^2(n+1)}.
	\end{equation}
	Since $\{a(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ satisfies 
	\ref{GenGORZThm1assump1} with $|j|\le 2$, \ref{GenGORZThm1assump2}, and \ref{genthmassump2}, we have, by  \Cref{newlem1}, 
	\[
	\frac{L_1(a)(n)}{a^2(n+1)}\sim 
	2{\delta}^2(n)\ \ (\text{as}\ n\to \infty).
	\]
	Plugging this into \eqref{Inflogconcaveeqn1} and using \ref{InflogconcaveThmassump1} with $j=\pm 1$, \ref{InflogconcaveThmassump2}, and \ref{InflogconcaveThmassump3}, we obtain
	\begin{equation}\label{Inflogeqn5}
	\mathcal{L}^{[1]}(a)(n)\sim 2{\delta}^2(n)a^2(n)\ \ (\text{as}\ n\to \infty).
	\end{equation}
	
	We now prove the theorem by induction on $r\in \mathbb{N}$. Using \eqref{Inflogeqn5}, it holds for $r=1$. Assume next that the theorem holds for $r$. Define $a_r(n):=\mathcal{L}^{[r]}(a)(n)$. By induction hypothesis,
	\begin{equation}\label{Indhyp}
	a_r(n)\sim  2^{2^{r+1}-r-2}{\delta}(n)^{2^{r+1}-2} a^{2^r}\!(n). 
	\end{equation}
 Therefore, using \eqref{Indhyp}, \Cref{Fact1}, \ref{GenGORZThm1assump1}, and \ref{InflogconcaveThmassump1},                                                                   
	$\{a_r(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ satisfies \ref{GenGORZThm1assump1} with $j=\pm 1$, \ref{GenGORZThm1assump2}, and \ref{genthmassump2} with $A_r(n):=(2^{r+1}-2)B(n)+2^rA(n)$ and ${\delta}_r(n):=\sqrt{2^r{\delta}^2(n)-\left(2^{r+1}-2\right)\beta^2(n)}$. Note that ${\delta}_r(n)\sim 2^{\frac r2}{\delta}(n)$ as $n\to \infty$. Moreover, employing \Cref{Fact1}, $\{{\delta}_r(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ satisfies \ref{InflogconcaveThmassump1} with $j=\pm 1$, \ref{InflogconcaveThmassump2}, and \ref{InflogconcaveThmassump3}. Using \eqref{Inflogeqn5} and \eqref{Indhyp}, the theorem holds for $r+1$.\qedhere
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- lemma-11: body_md -->
\label{Inftlogconcave:lem}
Let $\{a_d(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ be as in \eqref{genexample}. For $r\in \mathbb{N}$, we have,  as $n\to \infty$,
	\[
	\mathcal{L}^{[r]}(a_d)(n)\sim 2^{2^r-r-1}c_1^{2^r}(d)\left(\lambda^*\left(1-\lambda^*\right)A_{\lambda^*}(d)\right)^{2^r-1}\frac{\exp\left(2^r\sum_{\lambda\in \mathcal{S}}A_{\lambda}(d)n^{\lambda}\right)}{n^{2^rc_2(d)+(2^r-1)(2-\lambda^*)}}.
	\]
<!-- end lemma-11 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
Using \Cref{fact2} \ref{fact2part1}, $\{a_d(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ satisfies \ref{GenGORZThm1assump1} with $|j|\le 2$, \ref{GenGORZThm1assump2}, and \ref{genthmassump2}. Moreover, by \Cref{fact2} \ref{fact2part2}, $\{{\delta}(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ satisfies \ref{InflogconcaveThmassump1} with $j=\pm 1$, \ref{InflogconcaveThmassump2}, and \ref{InflogconcaveThmassump3}. Using \Cref{InflogconcaveThm}, \eqref{impfact}, and \eqref{genexample}, we conclude the proof.\qedhere
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
Applying \Cref{Inftlogconcave:lem} to \eqref{pnasymp}, the claim follows.\qedhere
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label{propdet}
	For $r\in \mathbb{N}_{\ge 2}$, we have 
	\[
	\prod_{m=1}^{r}\left(1-e^{-m x}\right)\sim r! x^r\ \text{as}\ x\to 0.
	\]
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
By \eqref{det} and \ref{GenGORZThm1assump1} with $|j|\le r-1$, we have, as $n\to \infty$,
	\begin{align*}                
	&\frac{\operatorname{T}^{[r]}_a(n)}{a^{r}(n)}\sim \det\left(\left(e^{-\left(k-\ell\right)^2{\delta}^2(n)}\right)_{1\le k,\ell\le r}\right).
	\end{align*}
	Thus, to prove the theorem, it suffices to show that, as $n\to \infty$, 
	\begin{equation}\label{detthm3}
	\mathcal{T}_r(n):=\det\left(\left(e^{-\left(k-\ell\right)^2{\delta}^2(n)}\right)_{1\le k,\ell\le r}\right)\sim \frac{(r-1)!^r2^{\frac{r(r-1)}{2}}}{\prod_{j=2}^{r-1}j^{j}}{\delta}^{r(r-1)}(n).
	\end{equation}
	To prove this, we use induction on $r\in \mathbb{N}_{\ge 2}$. For $r=2$, \eqref{detthm3} holds by \ref{GenGORZThm1assump2}. Assume next that \eqref{detthm3} holds for some $r\ge 2$. From \cite{DP}, we have that
	\begin{align*}
	\mathcal{T}_{r+1}(n)
	&
	=\mathcal{T}_r(n)\prod_{m=1}^{r}\left(1-e^{-2m{\delta}^2(n)}\right).
	\end{align*}
 Using \Cref{propdet} and the induction hypothesis then gives that \eqref{detthm3} holds for $r+1$.\qedhere
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- corollary-8: body_md -->
\label{detmain1}
	Let $\{a_d(n)\}$ be as in \eqref{genexample}. As $n\to \infty$, we have
	\[
	\operatorname{T}^{[r]}_{a_d}(n)\sim \frac{(r-1)!^r\left(\lambda^*(1-\lambda^*)A_{\lambda^*}(d)\right)^{\frac{r(r-1)}{2}}c^r_1(d)}{\prod_{j=2}^{r-1}j^{j}}\frac{\exp\left(r\sum_{\lambda\in \mathcal{S}}A_{\lambda}(d)n^{\lambda}\right)}{n^{\left(1-\frac{\lambda^*}{2}\right)r(r-1)+c_2(d)r}}. 
	\]
<!-- end corollary-8 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
Applying \Cref{detmain1} with \eqref{pnasymp}, we conclude the proof.\qedhere
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
Applying \Cref{detmain1} with the asymptotics of $\overline{p}(n)$, we conclude the proof. \qedhere
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
Applying \Cref{detmain1} with \Cref{brokenlem1}, we obtain the first claim. For the remaining claims, we apply \Cref{detmain1} and \Cref{shiftediffthm}.\qedhere
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
We use induction on $k\in \mathbb{N}_0$.  The base case $k=0$ follows from \Cref{newlem1}. Assume next that the statement holds for $k\in \mathbb{N}_0$. Define $a_{k}(n):=L^{[k]}_1\left(L_r(a)\right)(n)$. Using \eqref{itlagdef}, we write $L^{[k+1]}_1(L_r(a))(n)=L^{[1]}_1(a_k(n))$.
By the induction hypothesis, 
\begin{align}\label{itlageqn2}
a_k(n)&\sim 
(2r-1)!!^{2^k}2^{ 2^{k+1}\left(r+1\right)-k-3}{\delta}(n)^{2^{k+1}\left(r+1\right)-2} a^{2^{k+1}}(n)\ \ (\text{as}\ n\to \infty).
\end{align}
 Therefore for $j=\pm 1$, by \Cref{Fact1}, \ref{InflogconcaveThmassump1}, and \ref{GenGORZThm1assump1}, we have as $n\to \infty$,
\begin{align*}
\log\left(\frac{a_k(n\pm 1)}{a(n)}\right)&=\pm\left(\left(2^{k+1}\left(r+1\right)-2\right)B(n)+2^{k+1}A(n)\right)\\
&\hspace{4 cm}-\left(2^{k+1}{\delta}^2(n)-\left(2^{k+1}\left(r+1\right)-2\right)\beta^2(n)\right)+o(1).
\end{align*}
Thus  $\{a_k(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ satisfies \ref{GenGORZThm1assump1} with $j=\pm 1$,  $A_k(n):=(2^{k+1}\left(r+1\right)-2)B(n)+ 2^{k+1} A(n)$, and ${\delta}_k(n):=\sqrt{2^{k+1}{\delta}^2(n)-(2^{k+1}(r+1)-2)\beta^2(n)}$. Using \ref{InflogconcaveThmassump3} and \ref{GenGORZThm1assump2}, \ref{GenGORZThm1assump2} holds for $\{{\delta}_k(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$. By \ref{genthmassump2} and \ref{InflogconcaveThmassump2}, $\{a_k(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ satisfies \ref{genthmassump2}. Using \Cref{newlem1} and the induction hypothesis then gives that \eqref{itlageqn2} holds for $k+1$.\qedhere
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- corollary-9: body_md -->
\label{itlagthm2}
Let $\{a_d(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ be as in \eqref{genexample}. For $k\in \mathbb{N}_0$ and $r\in \mathbb{N}$, we have, as $n\to \infty$,
\begin{align*}
L^{[k]}_1\left(L_r(a_d)\right)(n)&\sim (2r-1)!!^{2^k} 2^{2^k(r+1)-k-2}\left(\lambda^*(1-\lambda^*)A_{\lambda^*}(d)\right)^{2^k(r+1)-1} c^{2^{k+1}}_1(d)\\
&\hspace{6.5 cm}\times \frac{\exp\left(2^{k+1}\sum_{\lambda\in \mathcal{S}}A_{\lambda}(d)n^{\lambda}\right)}{n^{\left(2-\lambda^*\right)\left(2^k(r+1)-1\right)+2^{k+1}c_2(d)}}.
\end{align*}
<!-- end corollary-9 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
By \Cref{fact2} \ref{fact2part1}, $\{a_d(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ satisfies {\rm{\ref{GenGORZThm1assump1}}} with $|j|\le 2r$, {\rm{\ref{GenGORZThm1assump2}}}, and {\rm{\ref{genthmassump2}}}. By \Cref{fact2} \ref{fact2part2}, \ref{InflogconcaveThmassump1} with $|j|\le 1$, \ref{InflogconcaveThmassump2}, and \ref{InflogconcaveThmassump3} hold for $\{{\delta}(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$. Thus, applying \Cref{itlagthm1}, \eqref{impfact}, and \eqref{genexample}, we conclude the proof.\qedhere
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
Applying \Cref{itlagthm2} with \eqref{pnasymp}, the asymptotics of $\overline{p}$, and the asymptotics of $\textup{spt}(n)$ (see \cite{B}), we conclude the proof.\qedhere
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- lemma-12: body_md -->
\label{logdifflem1}
Let $\{g_d(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ be as in \eqref{loggenexample}. For $r\in \mathbb{N}$ and $0<h_2(d)<1$, we have,
	\[
		(-1)^{r+1}\Delta^{[r]}(g_d)(n)\sim \frac{h_1(d)h_2(d)\prod_{m=1}^{r-1}\left(r-m-h_2(d)\right)}{n^{r-h_2(d)}}\ \ \text{as}\ n\to \infty.
	\]
<!-- end lemma-12 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
We prove the lemma by induction on $r\in \mathbb{N}$. Using \eqref{loggenexample} and \Cref{Fact1}, we see that $\{g_d(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ satisfies \ref{GenGORZThm1assump1} with $|j|\le 1$, $A(n):=\frac{h_2(d)}{n}$, and  ${\delta}(n):=\sqrt{\frac{h_2(d)}{2}}\frac 1n$, \ref{GenGORZThm1assump2}, and \ref{genthmassump2}. Consequently, using \Cref{newsec4lem1} (with $h=r=1$) and \eqref{loggenexample}, we have, as $n\to \infty$,
	\begin{equation*}                        
	\Delta^{[1]}\left(g_d\right)(n)
	\sim \frac{h_1(d)h_2(d)}{n^{1-h_2(d)}}.
	\end{equation*}
 Thus, for $r=1$, the lemma holds. Next, assume by induction, that the lemma holds for $r\in \mathbb{N}$. Define  $g^{[r]}_d(n):=(-1)^{r+1}\Delta^{[r]}\left(g_d\right)(n)$. 
	Consequently, by \Cref{Fact1} and the definition of $\Delta^{[r]}(a)(n)$, the lemma holds for $r+1$.\qedhere
<!-- end proof-30 -->
<!-- lemma-13: body_md -->
\label{logdifflem2}
	Let $\{a_d(n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ be as in \eqref{genexample}. Then we have, as $n\to \infty$,
	\[
	(-1)^{r+1}\Delta^{[r]}\left(\log(a_d)\right)(n)\sim \frac{\lambda^*A_{\lambda^*}(d)\prod_{m=1}^{r-1}\left(r-m-\lambda^*\right)}{n^{r-\lambda^*}}.
	\]
<!-- end lemma-13 -->
<!-- proof-31: body_md -->
Note that if $f(n)\sim g(n)$, then $\log (f(n))= \log(g(n))(1+o(1))$ as $n\to \infty$ unless $g(n)\to 0$. Thus, using \eqref{genexample}, \ref{genexampleassump2}, and \ref{genexampleassump3}, we have, as $n \to \infty$, 
	\begin{align*}\nonumber 
	&\log(a_d(n))
	\sim A_{\lambda^*}(d)n^{\lambda^*}.
	\end{align*}
 Finally, using \ref{genexampleassump2}, \ref{genexampleassump3}, and  \Cref{logdifflem1}, we conclude the proof.\qedhere
<!-- end proof-31 -->
<!-- proof-32: body_md -->
Using \Cref{brokenlem1} and \Cref{logdifflem2}, we conclude the proof.\qedhere
<!-- end proof-32 -->
<!-- remarks-1: body_md -->
\leavevmode\par
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*, labelsep=0.5em]
                                                                  
 \item \noindent  In \Cref{genthm}, we assume {\rm{\ref{GenGORZThm1assump1}}}, {\rm{\ref{GenGORZThm1assump2}}}, and {\rm{\ref{genthmassump2}}}. Can one relax (or modify) {\rm{\ref{genthmassump2}}} to obtain more general results?
\item With additional assumptions, can one obtain secondary order asymptotics of $I^{[\bm{M}]}_{\bm{\rho},\bm{s}}(a)(n)$ as studied in Theorem~\ref{genthm}?
\item In this paper, we restrict to sequences $\{a(n)\}_{n \ge 0}$ with asymptotics of the shape \eqref{genexample}. Can one extend our results to combinatorial sequences whose asymptotics do not have this shape?
\item While condition {\rm{\ref{GenGORZThm1assump1}}} in Theorem~\ref{GenGORZcor1} underlies the ``generic'' situation of Hermite polynomial limits for (renormalized) Jensen polynomials, there are many other interesting phenomena for other combinatorial sequences. 
For instance, in \cite{GriffinSouth}, Griffin and South obtained another distinguished class of polynomials that encode the asymptotics of Jensen polynomials for Taylor coefficients of entire functions. Can a suitable framework be developed for ``non-Hermite'' phenomena like that uncovered by Griffin and South? 
\item 
Many of the results in this paper can be shown to follow for large classes of sequences including Fourier coefficients of weakly holomorphic modular forms. For instance, we show that \eqref{Briggsineq} eventually  holds 
for a sequence  of the shape  \eqref{genexample}. Weakly holomorphic modular forms automatically satisfy such conditions. It would be interesting to pin down which of our results hold for these, and for other natural classes of automorphic objects. 
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end remarks-1 -->
